To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1. the problem of estimating bottleneck capacity is ill-posed for paths with more than one congested node, 2. the problem of available bandwidth estimation is solvable for a single congested router, and 3. the solution for the latter problem is accurate under arbitrary (including bursty and non-stationary), cross-traffic.
the available bandwidth of an Internet link can be estimated with arbitrary accuracy using the packet-pair method under non-neglibible cross-traffic.

(i) the bottleneck capacity and the available bandwidth can be estimated with high accuracy using packet-pair measurements, and (ii) the accuracy of the estimators depends on the cross-traffic conditions, and is not affected by the packet-pair size.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a fundamental problem of estimating the available bandwidth of endto- end paths under non-neglible cross-traffic and presents several novel solutions to this problem.
the fundamental problem of estimating the available bandwidth in the Internet, and the paper presents the first rigorous mathematical results in this area.
developing accurate and robust methods for bandwidth estimation in a realistic setting.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the packet pair technique is a good estimator for a single bottleneck link and a bad one for a path with multiple congested routers.
, for a single congested link, we have a simple and accurate method for estimating the available bandwidth and capacity.
the packet-pair bandwidth estimation is not a panacea for the problem of estimating bottleneck link capacity or end-to-end path bandwidth.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the problem of bandwidth estimation is well understood for a single bottleneck link, but is still largely an open problem for more complicated topologies.
the estimation of the bottleneck capacity is a well-posed and solvable problem, while the estimation of the available bandwidth is possible under certain assumptions.
the packet-pair technique is a powerful and accurate tool for estimating the capacity of a single congesting router and the available bandwidth on a path with a single router.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, while accurate estimation of end-to-end path bandwidth is in general impossible, the problem becomes feasible when the bottleneck link can be identified and its cross-traffic can be approximated as renewal.
, in order for bandwidth estimation to be feasible, the cross-traffic must be non-stationary and non-renewal.
the problem of accurate bandwidth estimation is not as hopeless as it may seem at first.
